# Grid bodies share one virtualization window, so a second grid stops the first from repainting

## Context

Operator report on `apps/workstation`, 100k Matrix pane: clicking **+1 pulse** increments the Pulse cell three columns to the left, and it works for the first handful of rows only. Every later row in the **visible area** does nothing — no error, the button paints its press, the counter does not move.

**Reproduced and automated** before any diagnosis, per the operator's instruction. New spec: `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationRowActionNL.spec.mjs`.

```
rows whose own Pulse cell did not increment:
  neo-record-7 … neo-record-27       ← records 1-6 increment correctly
```

The cutoff is exact and reproducible: **records 1–6 work, 7 onward do not**, with no scrolling involved.

## The witness, and why it is shaped this way

- **Paired by `data-record-id`, never by row position.** The grid is buffered and recycles row nodes, so "row 7" is not a stable subject. Each button is matched to the Pulse cell of the *same record*.
- **The Pulse column index is derived from the header**, not hardcoded. The grid has eight columns (`#`, `Work item`, `State`, `Throughput`, `Pulse`, `Load`, `Living signal`, `Action`) and the operator's screenshot is horizontally scrolled. A guessed index reads a neighbouring *name* column, which never increments — so the spec reports every row as broken and reads exactly like a perfect witness while measuring nothing. An explicit guard asserts the resolved column holds a number.
- **`dispatchEvent('click')`, not `click()`.** The Matrix animates continuously (a 10/sec feed, an animated counter, live sparklines), so an ordinary click times out on actionability and `force: true` clicks the coordinates resolved a moment earlier, which the moving grid has since given to another row. Both failure modes make *every* row look broken, including the six that work.

Each of those three was a wrong turn on the way here; all three produce a convincing red for the wrong reason, which is why they are recorded rather than tidied away.

## What is NOT yet established

**The mechanism is unconfirmed, deliberately.** The obvious hypothesis is stale closures in pooled component cells: `ScalePane.mjs` declares `handler: () => record.counter++`, a closure over the record captured when the cell component is built, and that column already carries a pooling-collision comment (`dataField: 'timestamp'` was chosen because *"reusing `counter` would alias the AnimatedChange column's pooled cells"*).

**But the evidence does not fit cleanly**, and saying so is the point of this section:

- `grid/column/Component.mjs`'s recycle path **does** re-invoke the component factory with the new `data` and `set()` the resulting config, so a recycled cell should receive a fresh handler.
- More importantly, **no scrolling occurs in the repro**. Without scrolling nothing is recycled, so every visible cell was created fresh — which is the `Neo.create` branch, not the reuse branch.

So a pooling explanation has to account for why creation-time cells beyond the sixth behave differently. The number six is suspicious on its own and is the thread to pull.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — every row rendered in the visible area increments its own Pulse cell, asserted by record id on the running app.
- [ ] **AC-2** — red-first: the witness is red at the current head, naming the records that failed and showing the 1–6 / 7+ cutoff.
- [ ] **AC-3** — the mechanism is identified and named before the fix, not inferred from the fix working. A change that makes the symptom disappear without an explanation does not close this.
- [ ] **AC-4** — after scrolling, a recycled row's action still acts on the record it currently displays, not the one its cell was built for. The report is about the initial viewport; recycling is the adjacent case and must not be left untested.
- [ ] **AC-5** — the existing dock and grid suites stay green at exact head.

## Out of Scope

- Rewriting the `component` column's pooling contract. If the defect turns out to live there, that is an engine ticket of its own with its own evidence.
- The `dataField: 'timestamp'` aliasing workaround already in `ScalePane`, unless the mechanism proves it to be the cause.

## Avoided Traps

- **Fixing the symptom by rebinding the handler on every render.** That would make the spec green while leaving the reason unknown, and would hide the same defect wherever else a component column is used.
- **Trusting the spec's red before checking what it measured.** Two of my three wrong turns produced a red on all 27 rows, which is more convincing than the true red and completely wrong.

## Related

- `apps/workstation/view/ScalePane.mjs` — the column definition and its existing pooling comment.
- `src/grid/column/Component.mjs` — the create/recycle paths.
- #17835 — scroll-edge on-demand loading for buffered surfaces.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-03T10:19:25Z

## Mechanism found. It is not the button, not the closure, and not the pooling.

Three measurements, each killing the hypothesis before it.

### 1. The handler is fine — the record increments for every row

Clicked three rows and read the **record** through the Neural Link rather than the DOM:

| record | store counter | Pulse cell |
|---|---|---|
| `neo-record-3` | 75 → **76** | 75 → **76** |
| `neo-record-7` | 73 → **74** | 73 → 73 |
| `neo-record-9` | 37 → **38** | 37 → 37 |

The counter advances on **every** row. `record.counter++` runs, the model updates, the store fires. Only the paint is missing. That rules out the stale-closure hypothesis this ticket was filed on, and with it the `component`-column pooling theory.

Corroborated independently: 27 rows, 27 action buttons, **zero duplicate button ids**. Each row owns a distinct Button whose handler closes over the right record.

### 2. It is positional, not ordinal — the click order was a confound

The report and my first witness both clicked top-to-bottom, so "the first six rows" and "the first six clicks" were indistinguishable. Clicking in **reverse** (record 27 → 1) separates them:

```
passed: neo-record-6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1
failed: neo-record-27, 26, 25 … 8, 7
```

Records 7–27 fail even when clicked *first*. Rows 1–6 work even when clicked *last*. The cutoff is the store index, and nothing else.

### 3. The grid believes six rows are mounted while twenty-seven are painted

`Neo.grid.Body` for the scale pane, read live after settle:

```
rowPoolSize    : 27          ← pool is correct
availableRows  : 7
bufferRowRange : 10
mountedRows    : [0, 5]      ← six
visibleRows    : [0, 1]      ← two
DOM rows        : 27
```

`rowPoolSize` is right (`7 + 2×10 = 27`, and 27 rows are in the DOM). **`mountedRows` is `[0, 5]`.** Both repaint paths gate on it, and both drop everything above it with no else branch:

- `src/grid/Body.mjs:1310` — `onStoreRecordChange()`: `if (rowIndex >= mountedRows[0] && rowIndex <= mountedRows[1])` → `row.createVdom(false, false)`. This is the path that paints the new value.
- `src/grid/Body.mjs:1141` — `getRow()`: the same guard, returning `null` above the window. `grid/column/AnimatedChange.mjs:60` then does `if (row) {…}` and silently does nothing, which is why the animation is missing too.

A record change at store index ≥ 6 is discarded in both. No error, no warning — exactly the reported symptom of a button that visibly presses and changes nothing.

`availableRows: 7` and `visibleRows: [0, 1]` are the same staleness seen from other angles: the pane is ~1350px of painted rows, so a settled measurement would put `availableRows` near 27, not 7. The pool was resized to 27; the window bookkeeping that feeds these three configs was not.

### Why `examples/grid/bigData` works

@tobiu pointed at it as a working control, and the comparison is what makes the shape clear. That grid has the same column pair — a `component` column with `handler() {record.counter++}` and an `animatedChange` column on `counter` — and it works for every row. It is not laid out inside a dock that resizes after mount. The Workstation's scale grid measures its viewport once at a small early size, the dock then gives it its real height, and `mountedRows` never catches up.

So the difference is not in the column definitions and not in `ScalePane.mjs`. **The `dataField: 'timestamp'` workaround in `ScalePane` is unrelated to this defect** and should not be touched while fixing it.

### What this changes about the ticket

AC-3 asked for the mechanism before the fix; it is now named, so the fix has a target: **the mounted-row window must be recomputed when the grid's height changes after mount.** The remaining open question is which layer owns that — whether the dock fails to notify on resize, or the body fails to remeasure on a notification it does receive. That is the next measurement, not a guess to encode in a fix.

AC-4 (recycling after scroll) stands unchanged and is still worth its arm: it covers the adjacent case this one does not.

One correction to my own framing above the fold: this ticket's title says the action "increments only the first six rows". More precisely, **it increments every row; only the first six repaint.** The record is always right. Anything reading the store — a save, a sort, an export — already sees the correct value, which makes this a display defect with a data-correct model underneath, and narrows the blast radius accordingly.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-03T10:55:32Z

Closing as Drop+Supersede per @tobiu, alongside PRs #18190 and #18191.

The symptom this ticket describes is real and reproduces: on a page with two grids, the smaller grid's window overwrites the larger one's and every row outside the borrowed window silently stops repainting. But the ticket is scoped as a Workstation grid bug, and it is not one — it is one caller of a class-config-system gap, and scoping the lane here is what led me to two consumer-level fixes that both deserved to be dropped.

Superseded by #18192, which states the defect where it lives and carries the minimal reproduction: a `clone` descriptor is silently inert on a non-reactive config, which has no other protection from sharing. Witness in #18194.

Nothing is lost by closing this. The diagnosis is reproduced in full on #18192, and the grid's own follow-up — its three window arrays are not configuration at all, since nothing anywhere passes them as instance config — is recorded there as an explicitly separate lane rather than being smuggled into the config fix.
